notes: §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 SR1 (as Amendment 2 replaced it), for every word but LENGTH, RANDOM and SUM: "Reserved words form disjoint sets with user-defined words, system-names, and function-names" and "The same COBOL word may be used as a function-name, as a system-name, and as a user-defined word. The classification of a specific occurrence of such COBOL words is determined by the context of the clause or phrase in which it occurs." Part (a): the generated reserved-word table carries a per-edition flag (ReservedWordEntry.IsReservedAt, the 85 arm reads R85) whose R85 set is exactly the 350 words of the list at §1985:IV.8 with FUNCTION (compared mechanically, no word on either side alone); a reserved word is a keyword token, never an IDENTIFIER, the name slots admit a gated one only where AdmitsAsUserWord says the edition leaves it free (userWordHere), and a reserved one written as a name is reported COBOL0901 by the funnel (VisitReservedGatedWord and FlagReservedUserWord over RejectsAt) or by the parser's listener (ReservedUserWordViolation). Probed at --std 85: each of the 350 words is refused as a data-name (declared, referenced, subscripted, qualified), paragraph-name, section-name, program-name, condition-name, index-name, file-name, alphabet-name, class-name, symbolic-character, mnemonic-name and computer-name (a system-name). Part (b): no function-name of the 1989 module other than the three excluded words has a table row, so it lexes as a user-defined word everywhere and is a function-name only after FUNCTION (functionCall reads functionName there); the 2023 refusal of a function-name as a user-defined word (DeclareUserWord) hangs on a REPOSITORY function-specifier, which no 1985 program has. Probed at --std 85: each of the 39 other function-names is accepted in all twelve of those slots. The witness declares MAX, MIN, UPPER-CASE, REVERSE, INTEGER, NUMVAL and the paragraph MOD and references each as the function and as the user-defined word in one statement.

next.reason: §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 SR1 (the paragraph as Amendment 2, X3.23b-1993, replaced it; Errata C198): "For all COBOL words excluding the words LENGTH, RANDOM, and SUM: a. Reserved words form disjoint sets with user-defined words, system-names, and function-names. b. ... The same COBOL word may be used as a function-name, as a system-name, and as a user-defined word." 2023 keeps (a) against user-defined words and system-names, §2023:8.3.2.1 SR1 "Reserved words shall not be used as user-defined words or system-names", and (b) between system-names and user-defined words, §2023:8.3.2.1 SR4 "A given word may be used as a system-name and as a user-defined word". The function-name part has a different requirement, §2023:8.3.2.1 SR5: "Intrinsic-function-names may be used as user-defined words and system-names, except for — intrinsic function names LENGTH, RANDOM, SIGN, and SUM; and — intrinsic function names identified in a function-specifier in the REPOSITORY paragraph." The words that differ: "SIGN", a fourth word that is both reserved (§2023:8.9) and an intrinsic function name (§2023:8.11), where 1985 excludes three; and the added case "identified in a function-specifier in the REPOSITORY paragraph", in which a function-name may NOT be a user-defined word or a system-name, where 1985 lets every function-name outside the three be one. 2023 has no rule of its own for the 1985 sentence that context determines the classification.
